page: Google Cloud Platform c4d-highmem-8-lssd is a general-purpose, memory-skewed virtual machine instance configured with AMD EPYC 9B45 processors based on the x86_64 architecture. The server provides 8 dedicated vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The cache topology includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. Memory capacity is allocated at 63.0 GB, yielding a high density of 7.88 GB of RAM per vCPU. The hardware setup includes a bundled 402 GB local NVMe SSD for high-speed ephemeral storage, contains zero discrete GPUs, and provides no complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations reveal distinct performance advantages in single-threaded compute tasks. The instance scored 3,459.89 points in the stress-ng single-core test, placing it in the top 10% tier across comparable cloud servers. Single-threaded throughput tests similarly demonstrated top-tier speeds, registering 37.53 GB/sec in gzip compression and 16.88 GB/sec in bzip3 decompression. Multi-core performance aligns with midrange tier expectations for an 8-vCPU system, achieving 13,816.23 points in multi-core stress-ng and 17,625.28 points in the overall PassMark CPU score. Uncached memory bandwidth measured 48.77 GB/sec for reads and 33.56 GB/sec for writes.

Hardware-level vector and cryptography extensions are supported, including AVX-512, AVX512-VNNI, AVX-VNNI, SHA-NI, and VAES instructions, aiding compute density for specialized mathematical and encryption workloads. Given the combination of fast local NVMe storage, top-tier single-core execution speed, and an elevated RAM allocation, this instance suits in-memory databases, Redis caching clusters, CI/CD artifact handling, data transformation pipelines, and relational database hosting requiring local scratch storage.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4d-highmem-8-lssd provides 8 dedicated vCPUs and 63.0 GB of RAM powered by an AMD EPYC 9B45 x86_64 processor across 4 physical cores. It features a bundled 402 GB local NVMe SSD and excludes discrete GPUs. Benchmark results highlight top-tier single-core performance, achieving 3,459.89 in stress-ng single-core tests along with top-tier single-threaded compression speeds of 37.53 GB/sec in gzip and 16.88 GB/sec in bzip3. Multi-threaded workloads and memory throughput place in the middle 50% tier, with a PassMark CPU score of 17,625.28 and Redis SET throughput reaching 14.96 million operations per second. Hardware support includes AVX-512, AVX-VNNI, and VAES encryption instructions. With 7.88 GB of RAM per vCPU combined with integrated NVMe local storage, the instance is structured for memory-heavy computing, caching layers, database workloads, and data processing tasks requiring responsive single-thread throughput.
